title: Best workflow/tool to generate a cohesive isometric pixel art tilemap with AI? PixelLab props are great, terrain tiles aren’t
author: charlycharlychar
selftext:
Hi! I’m working on a small browser game with an isometric pixel art map (zoomable and pannable).

What’s working: PixelLab for props and characters (64x64, isometric, 8 directions). I’m happy with those. Screenshots attached.

What’s not working: terrain tiles. I need grass, cobblestone, dirt paths, water and the transitions between them, in the same style, palette and 2:1 isometric angle as the props. I’ve tried:

* PixelLab’s terrain tools: the quality doesn’t match the props, and the tiles show seams.
* ChatGPT image generation: inconsistent angles, not real pixel art, and nothing tiles properly.

As a test I also generated the ground procedurally with code. It’s seamless but looks a bit flat (screenshot attached).

Questions:

1. What’s your workflow for AI-generated isometric terrain tilesets that actually tile and match existing assets? Tools, models, LoRAs or prompting tricks?
2. Is it better to generate tiles (Wang/blob tilesets for Tiled) or a whole map image and slice it?
3. Or is the realistic answer “AI for props, hand-made or procedural for terrain”? Any recommended packs in this style (sage greens, cream stone, warm wood)?

Target: 2:1 isometric, 64x32 ground tiles, limited palette, light from the top-left.

Thanks!

comments.author: Disastrous-Round-150
comments.body: Stop wasting time on game assets! Go 100% procedural! 🔥
